collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The red feathers for the harvest ceremony have become scarce: use something else, or skip the ceremony until they return.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The harvest ceremony has always used red feathers, but the red birds have become rare, and there are hardly any feathers left. (friend) suggests using red flowers instead. (subject) says flowers would change the meaning. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The ceremony is held with red flowers. Some elders refuse to take part. Most people find it beautiful. Over the years, the flowers become part of the meaning, and the red birds, left alone, slowly come back.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village skips the ceremony for a year, and leaves the red birds in peace. It feels strange and empty. The next year, a few feathers are found, and the ceremony is held, smaller and more precious than before.
